_comment: Hinglish phrase meanings. Must stay consistent with AI-spec.md section 4 (ask when ambiguous; days vs nights; no couple from head count).

phrases.title: kal
phrases.content: 'kal' can mean yesterday or tomorrow. Unless the context makes it clear, ask which date the user means.

phrases.title: parso
phrases.content: 'parso' can mean the day before yesterday or the day after tomorrow. Unless the context makes it clear, ask which date the user means.

phrases.title: agle hafte
phrases.content: 'agle hafte' / 'next week' names a week, not exact dates. Ask for the exact start and end dates.

phrases.title: is hafte
phrases.content: 'is hafte' means this week; it does not give exact dates. Ask for the exact start and end dates.

phrases.title: agle mahine
phrases.content: 'agle mahine' / 'next month' names a month, not exact dates. Ask for the exact dates.

phrases.title: din (days)
phrases.content: 'N din' means N days including the start day: end = start + N - 1 (do=2, teen=3, char=4, paanch=5).

phrases.title: raat (nights)
phrases.content: 'N raat' means N nights: end = start + N days (do=2, teen=3, char=4).

phrases.title: ek hafta
phrases.content: 'ek hafta' (one week) means 7 days including the start day: end = start + 6 days. Ask if the user may mean 7 nights.

phrases.title: family
phrases.content: Travelling with family members, children or parents ('ghar wale', 'bacchon ke saath', 'mummy papa') means trip_type family.

phrases.title: couple
phrases.content: Travelling with a spouse or partner ('biwi', 'patni', 'pati', girlfriend, boyfriend) means trip_type couple.

phrases.title: friends
phrases.content: Travelling with friends ('dosto ke saath', 'yaar log') means trip_type group_of_friends.

phrases.title: hum dono
phrases.content: 'hum dono' / 'do log' means two people but does NOT establish couple. Ask who is travelling.

phrases.title: chhutti
phrases.content: 'chhutti' means holiday or leave. If a festival is named, use its REFERENCE NOTES date; otherwise ask for exact dates.
